newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end up led by mining sector's bull run.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end up led by mining sector's bull run.

text.p: For the fourth time in the last five sessions, gains in the mining sector led the Lima stock exchange to a higher close Tuesday due to elevated international metal prices, brokers said.
While the sector could see some technical corrections Wednesday, players expect a mixed session as electricity stocks were seen attracting buyers, they added.
Tuesday, the General Index rose 0.89 percent to 1,740.88 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index climbed 1.06 percent to 2,514.02 points.
In a total of 1,603 trades, volume was 27.7 million soles ($10.5 million), according to preliminary figures.
"Mining stocks are rising because of higher metal prices and the fact that the (international) supply of zinc has fallen," Javier Alvares of local brokerage Finanval said.
Peruvian mining companies have a special advantage of generally being polymetal producers, which means they can take advantage of price rises in various metals, Aldo Quintana of Interfip said.
Polymetal miner Buenaventura was the most heavily traded stock Tuesday with 24.6 percent of the day's total trade. Peru's leading miner rose 1.26 perecnt to 24.10 soles.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru remained stable at 6.31 soles in continued modest volume that represented only eight percent of the day's trade.
Electricity distributor, Moyopampa -- formerly known as Edegel -- rose 4.27 percent to 1.25 soles, in nine percent of the day's total volume.
